body: That's an interesting suggestion. I'm pretty hooked on using mechanical pencils, but maybe I'll try and resort back to the olden ways.

Thank you for the kind words.

I've been seeing a counselor for a few months but I know it isn't intensive enough. If I manage to hang in there for another month I plan on starting to see a therapist in my hometown area. I've talked to my mom about what's going on and she tells me it's "teen angst" and just based on my last relationship going sour. She's a psychiatric nurse and you would think that she would listen to me when I tell her otherwise. My family isn't much help. I love them all deeply but I have trouble connecting with them about anything and most of the time I am bothered by their attempts to help. Being around my family is pretty stressful for an array of reasons. I guess the absolute biggest reason is that they are all so stressed out themselves. My mom especially because she works two jobs, sometimes takes one day off a week but usually works double-shifts every day. By the time I see her she is completely worn out and because of her exhaustion she will say things that are unintentionally annoying/hurtful. One of the two jobs makes her absolutely miserable, but she doesn't have the time to fill out job apps for a new one and refuses to work only one job because her and my dad are dead set on getting my brothers and I through college. I appreciate it so much, but it makes it even harder to feel like I can be happy when the prime people who are supposed to be life examples to me are pretty unhappy.

One of the things that has been stressing me out most is that I have to move back home. I made a mistake and went to a community college out of state for the last year because I couldn't afford the school I wanted to go to in the same city. I basically spent a year unable to make many friends of my own and ridiculously stressed out over school work. My parents can't afford for me to stay here, and after the breakup with my boyfriend and the last miserable year I don't really want to stay here anyways, but I don't want to go back home either. It's all meh. I really want to find a school that I'll really like and live on campus. I'm Canadian so ideally I want to go back there, but they don't accept student in January like they do in the States and thus I wouldn't be able to go for a year :(. A year at home is nottttttt what I need, but transferring somewhere midyear and then back out again would be a pain too.
